classification: public aggregate results; raw corpus bytes are not embedded
research_question: Does a staged short-program search improve complete stored size across held-out real data and multiple codecs?

sampling.method: smallest lexicographic (SHA-256(frame), offset) among complete non-overlapping frames per source file

program_language.proxy: descriptor bytes + zlib level-1 stream bytes

frame_contract.outer_metadata: codec, original length, and frame boundary are supplied by the outer object

limitations: Silesia is a fixed public benchmark, not a sample of the user's future production distribution.
Canterbury informed the transform language; only Silesia is treated as held-out in this run.
The audit covers the fixed 285-program language and 12 selected 4 KiB frames, not arbitrary programs.
Encoder and decoder timings are machine-specific Python measurements; stored-size results are exact.
The outer object metadata named in the frame contract is not counted because it is common to baseline and staged frames.
